chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'What the fasting person does will not harm him, provided he avoids three things: food, drink, and women, and submerging himself in water.'
ai.seo_question: What are the three things that invalidate a fast according to Imam Abu Ja'far?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Istibsar, Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies that the validity of the fast remains intact provided the fasting person avoids the three primary nullifiers—eating, drinking, and sexual intercourse—along with submerging in water (al--irtimas). This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between major acts that break the fast and other actions that may be disliked or require precaution but do not invalidate it, emphasizing the preservation of the fast's core spiritual integrity.
